No, actually. Things would not be more affordable. There would be fewer things to buy. Those things which were available to buy would have lower prices, but paradoxically would also likely be less affordable.

There would be a time of changeover, but I don't know if it would be any different - you save a little here and there BEFORE the purchase, rather than pay a little here and there AFTER the purchase.

I think that the only difference would be that you would have to wait to make that purchase, so the economy would take that time hit, as people transitioned, but I am not so sure it would a huge effect. I suppose that if people had to start saving first, rather than get the instant gratification of the credit purchase (something for nothing, or at least something NOW for a future something), they might purchase less, which would have a dampening effect on the economy.
